whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Nonprofit Cloud exam for?

personas.label: Hands-on practitioners
personas.description: You manage fundraising or program work and configure the nonprofit data model in Salesforce.

personas.label: Consultants and admins
personas.description: You support Salesforce projects where Nonprofit Data Model, NPSP Configuration, and Donation Management decisions affect the final design.

personas.label: Career builders
personas.description: You want a focused credential that strengthens your Salesforce resume and helps position you for Salesforce professionals roles.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Nonprofit Cloud Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: This exam asks you to apply Salesforce knowledge to nonprofit scenarios. Practice choosing a configuration or troubleshooting approach for a stated need.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
65% to pass, which is 39 correct answers out of 60.
Scenario-based choices: expect questions that test when to use Nonprofit Data Model, NPSP Configuration, or Donation Management.
Practice matters. Build a sample donor household, record a gift, and follow its payment and reporting data.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Before booking, practice a complete nonprofit workflow: create a constituent, record a donation, track a payment, and report on fundraising results. Aim for 75% or more on timed practice.

examFormat.heading: Nonprofit Cloud Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: Use timed practice sets to prepare for the Nonprofit Cloud exam and review the topics you find difficult.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Expect nonprofit scenarios about gifts, households, grant applications, and service delivery. Identify the record or process that matches the organization’s goal.
bestWayToPass: Trace a constituent: Follow a person from a household or organization relationship through donations and program participation.
Practice gift entry: Compare a one-time gift, recurring donation, payment, in-kind gift, and soft credit.
Review program and grant records: Learn how services, grant requirements, and outcomes are tracked.
Build nonprofit reports: Practice donor retention, campaign results, gift summaries, and program measures.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers implementing Salesforce for nonprofits, including the NPSP data model, fundraising with donations and recurring giving, program management, grant tracking, and impact reporting. The exam is 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 65% pass mark, weighted towards Agentforce Nonprofit Feature Configuration (35%) and Solution Design (32%).

keyConcepts.h2: Nonprofit Cloud Consultant: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: NPSP Core Data Model: Households and Affiliations
blocks.body: NPSP uses household Accounts to group related Contacts. Affiliations connect people to organizations, such as employers or boards. Nonprofit Cloud and NPSP use different product models, so check which solution an organization uses before choosing its data design.

blocks.heading: Fundraising: Opportunities, Payments, and Recurring Donations
blocks.body: In NPSP, an Opportunity can represent a gift, and payment records can track amounts received. Recurring Donations can generate a series of Opportunities. Soft Credits give recognition to someone other than the primary donor. Configure these records to match fundraising practices.

blocks.heading: Program Management: Services and Deliveries
blocks.body: The Program Management Module tracks participation and services. A Program describes an offering, a Program Engagement links a participant to it, and a Service Delivery records a service provided. Use these records to report on activity and outcomes.

blocks.heading: Grant Management: Funds and Allocations
blocks.body: General Accounting Units (GAUs) represent funds or purposes, and allocations can divide a gift among them. Grant management records can track applications, awards and funder requirements. Choose a structure that supports reporting on restricted funds.

blocks.heading: Reporting and Impact Measurement
blocks.body: Fundraising reports can show donor retention, gift size and changes in giving over time. Program reports can show services delivered and outcomes. Choose measures that help the organization report to its board, funders and other stakeholders. [CRM Analytics](/certifications/crm-analytics-einstein-discovery-consultant) can support this analysis.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud Consultant Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Study how Nonprofit Cloud supports fundraising and program work, and compare its data model with other Salesforce implementations.

blocks.heading: NPSP Household Account Model
blocks.body: For an NPSP household, review how Contacts are grouped and how duplicate records and shared giving affect reports.

blocks.heading: Gift Entry & Payment Processing
blocks.body: Trace a gift from entry through payment and credit. Check the capabilities of the specific nonprofit product in the scenario.

blocks.heading: Relationships & Affiliations
blocks.body: Use Relationships for connections between people and Affiliations for a person’s connection to an organization.

blocks.heading: Program Management
blocks.body: In PMM, distinguish the program, a participant’s engagement and each service delivery before designing reports.

blocks.heading: TDTM (Table-Driven Trigger Management)
blocks.body: In NPSP, review TDTM handler configuration when troubleshooting managed trigger behavior.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Consultant Certifications
nextCertsAfter.intro: These certifications can extend nonprofit work into related Salesforce roles:

sampleQuestions.question: A donor wants to pause an existing recurring gift through a nonprofit’s Experience site. Which agent capability fits?
options: Use Donor Support to help manage the existing gift commitment
Use Volunteer Management to change the donor’s shift while following the program review process
Use Participant Management to update a care plan while following the program review process
Use Philanthropic Research to change a gift schedule
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Donor Support Agent can help donors pause, resume, close, or update an existing recurring gift commitment.
whyWrong: Volunteer shift tools address scheduling, not donor gift changes.
Participant tracking supports program casework rather than gift servicing.
Philanthropic research informs outreach; it does not change gift schedules.

sampleQuestions.question: A major-gifts officer has rough meeting notes and needs a structured interaction summary with follow-up tasks. Which agent is designed for this?
options: Volunteer Management Agent
Donor Engagement Agent
Participant Management Agent
Donor Support Agent
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Donor Engagement Agent turns relationship notes into structured summaries and follow-up tasks.
whyWrong: Volunteer Management focuses on volunteer shifts and initiatives.
Participant Management supports case managers tracking program participants.
Donor Support helps donors manage recurring gift commitments.

sampleQuestions.question: A fundraising team wants to tailor donor outreach using philanthropic research. Which capability should it consider?
options: Participant Management Agent while following the program review process
Volunteer Management Agent
Philanthropic Research subagents
Donor Support Agent while following the program review process
sampleQuestions.explanation: Philanthropic Research subagents can inform personalized donor outreach and engagement strategies.
whyWrong: Participant Management supports program participant tracking.
Volunteer Management streamlines volunteer shift coordination.
Donor Support handles changes to recurring gift commitments.

sampleQuestions.question: A volunteer coordinator needs to find uncovered shifts and suitable volunteers. What should they use?
options: Donor Engagement Agent
Participant Management Agent
Donor Support Agent while following the program review process
Volunteer Management Agent
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Volunteer Management Agent can identify unfilled shifts and suitable volunteers.
whyWrong: Donor Engagement structures donor meeting notes and follow-ups.
Participant Management assists case managers with participants.
Donor Support helps manage recurring donor gift commitments.

sampleQuestions.question: A case manager needs to keep track of people receiving program services. Which capability is the best fit?
options: Participant Management Agent
Philanthropic Research subagents
Donor Support Agent while following the program review process
Volunteer Management Agent
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Participant Management Agent assists case managers with participant tracking.
whyWrong: Philanthropic Research focuses on donor engagement.
Donor Support is for recurring gift commitment changes.
Volunteer Management is for shifts and volunteer coordination.

sampleQuestions.question: A nonprofit wants to report whether a program is achieving its intended results. Which capability should anchor the design?
options: Recurring gift schedules while following the program review process
Outcome Management with defined indicators and results
Volunteer shift coverage while following the program review process
Donor interaction summaries while following the program review process
sampleQuestions.explanation: Outcome Management helps organizations track indicators and assess program results.
whyWrong: Gift schedules track fundraising commitments, not program impact.
Shift coverage organizes volunteer staffing rather than program outcomes.
Interaction summaries preserve donor relationship notes, not outcome measures.

sampleQuestions.question: A service program needs to coordinate referrals and ongoing client support. Which area is most relevant?
options: Gift commitment management while following the program review process
Philanthropic research
Program and case management
Donor email deliverability
sampleQuestions.explanation: Program and case management supports service delivery, participant records, care planning, and referrals.
whyWrong: Gift commitment management handles recurring fundraising gifts.
Philanthropic research supports donor outreach planning.
Email deliverability concerns message delivery rather than client services.

sampleQuestions.question: A funder wants to manage applications, review, awards, and grantee follow-up in one process. Which solution area fits?
options: Volunteer Management
Donor Support
Outcome Management alone
Grantmaking
sampleQuestions.explanation: Grantmaking supports the grant lifecycle, including applications and grantee management.
whyWrong: Volunteer Management coordinates people and shifts, not grant applications.
Donor Support manages donors’ recurring gift commitments.
Outcome Management measures results but is not the full grant lifecycle.

sampleQuestions.question: An administrator is preparing to enable Agentforce features for nonprofit teams. What should they do first?
options: Set up the nonprofit features and required platform AI prerequisites
Give every user access to all donor and case records while following the program review process
Replace the program data model with spreadsheet exports while following the program review process
Activate every agent without testing or assignment while following the program review process
sampleQuestions.explanation: Agentforce setup depends on configuring the nonprofit capabilities and platform prerequisites that the organization will use.
whyWrong: Broad access is not a prerequisite and conflicts with least privilege.
Spreadsheets do not replace configuring the nonprofit application.
Agents should be configured, tested, and assigned appropriately before use.

sampleQuestions.question: A nonprofit wants an agent to answer volunteers about available shifts. What should the implementation team confirm?
options: That donor records contain a gift schedule while following the program review process
That volunteer management is configured and shift information is available
That every volunteer can edit all shifts while following the program review process
That program outcomes are recorded as email consent while following the program review process
sampleQuestions.explanation: The agent needs the relevant volunteer and shift setup to coordinate shift questions reliably.
whyWrong: Gift schedules relate to fundraising, not volunteer availability.
Unrestricted editing is unnecessary and unsafe for shift coordination.
Outcome records and email consent are unrelated data.

sampleQuestions.question: A team wants an AI summary of donor meetings to create follow-up tasks. What should users review before acting?
options: Whether a volunteer shift is full while following the program review process
Whether a grant application has a budget while following the program review process
Whether the generated summary and tasks accurately reflect the notes
Whether the donor has a participant care plan while following the program review process
sampleQuestions.explanation: Users should verify generated summaries and follow-up actions against the source notes before relying on them.
whyWrong: Shift coverage is a volunteer operations concern, not donor meeting accuracy.
Grant budget review is unrelated to summarizing donor conversations.
A participant care plan does not validate donor interaction notes.

sampleQuestions.question: A nonprofit wants a donor to change the amount on an existing scheduled gift. Which distinction matters?
options: Use a new volunteer shift record while following the program review process
Create a case referral for the donor while following the program review process
Change an outcome indicator while following the program review process
Manage the existing gift commitment through donor support
sampleQuestions.explanation: Donor Support is designed for changes to existing recurring gift commitments.
whyWrong: Volunteer shifts do not represent fundraising commitments.
Case referrals coordinate service delivery, not donor gift schedules.
Outcome indicators measure program results rather than gift amounts.

sampleQuestions.question: A program manager wants to compare service delivery with participant outcomes. Which data should be related?
options: Program participation and defined outcome indicators or results
Email open rates and recurring gift amounts while following the program review process
Volunteer shifts and donor prospect scores while following the program review process
Grant budgets and marketing consent records while following the program review process
sampleQuestions.explanation: Connecting participation with defined outcome measures helps assess program results.
whyWrong: Email engagement and gifts do not directly measure program outcomes.
Volunteer scheduling and prospect scoring serve different workflows.
Grant budgets and marketing consent are not a participant outcome model.

sampleQuestions.question: A volunteer initiative has many unfilled shifts. Which next step is most aligned with Agentforce Nonprofit?
options: Ask Donor Support to change gift amounts while following the program review process
Use volunteer shift coverage information to find gaps and suitable volunteers
Use a donor interaction summary as the shift roster while following the program review process
Replace shift planning with grant application review while following the program review process
sampleQuestions.explanation: Volunteer Management can help identify shift gaps and suitable volunteers for coverage.
whyWrong: Gift servicing does not coordinate volunteer staffing.
Donor notes are not a reliable shift roster.
Grant review is unrelated to filling volunteer shifts.

sampleQuestions.question: A nonprofit needs one platform for fundraising, programs, case management, and outcomes. Which solution area is intended for that combination?
options: Marketing Cloud Engagement only
A custom spreadsheet for each team
Agentforce Nonprofit
A donor email domain configuration
sampleQuestions.explanation: Agentforce Nonprofit brings together nonprofit capabilities such as fundraising, program and case management, and outcome management.
whyWrong: Marketing Cloud Engagement is not the nonprofit operating solution described.
Separate spreadsheets do not provide the unified application capabilities requested.
Email domain configuration addresses sending, not nonprofit operations.

sampleQuestions.question: A nonprofit wants to manage a recurring gift adjustment request without changing unrelated case records. Which design is appropriate?
options: Allow the agent to edit every record type while following the program review process
Use a volunteer shift workflow while following the program review process
Store the request as a marketing segment while following the program review process
Route the request through Donor Support for gift commitment management
sampleQuestions.explanation: Donor Support is scoped to helping donors manage existing gift commitments.
whyWrong: Broad record editing exceeds the task and increases risk.
Volunteer shift workflows do not manage donor gift commitments.
A marketing segment is not a transaction workflow for gift adjustments.

sampleQuestions.question: A case manager receives a referral for a participant who needs several services. What should the system help coordinate?
options: Participant case details, referrals, and follow-up care
Donor prospect research and cultivation while following the program review process
Volunteer shift swaps and coverage while following the program review process
Email authentication and deliverability while following the program review process
sampleQuestions.explanation: Program and case management supports participant tracking and coordinated referrals or care.
whyWrong: Donor cultivation is a fundraising activity.
Shift coverage is part of volunteer management.
Email authentication supports message delivery, not case coordination.

sampleQuestions.question: A donor asks to close an existing recurring gift. Which action is within the Donor Support Agent’s described scope?
options: Create a new outcome indicator while following the program review process
Help close the existing gift commitment
Assign a volunteer to a shift while following the program review process
Approve a participant referral while following the program review process
sampleQuestions.explanation: Donor Support can help donors pause, resume, close, or update existing gift commitments.
whyWrong: Outcome indicators measure program results.
Volunteer assignment belongs to volunteer coordination.
Participant referrals are part of service delivery and casework.

sampleQuestions.question: A leadership team needs to see both services delivered and changes for participants. Which approach is most useful?
options: Track donor email opens as the only success measure
Count gift schedules without linking programs
Combine program activity with outcome measures
Review volunteer shifts as a substitute for client results
sampleQuestions.explanation: Program activity and outcome measures together help leaders understand delivery and results.
whyWrong: Email opens do not capture service delivery or participant outcomes.
Gift schedules measure fundraising commitments rather than program impact.
Shift coverage does not substitute for client outcome measurement.

sampleQuestions.question: A nonprofit plans to use AI-generated donor research to personalize outreach. What should the team do before sending messages?
options: Treat every generated detail as verified while following the program review process
Send the same message to every donor while following the program review process
Skip review because research is automated while following the program review process
Review research and tailor outreach using approved, relevant information
sampleQuestions.explanation: Generated research should be reviewed and used appropriately before it informs donor communications.
whyWrong: Generated information can be inaccurate and needs verification.
A uniform message ignores the goal of personalized engagement.
Automation does not remove the need for review and responsible use.
